To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcription of temperate Streptococcus phages in the prophage state was studied by Northern blot and RT-PCR experiments.
temperate phage from lactic strepococci encode a variable number genes that increase the ecological fitnes of the lysogen.

(1) the transcription of prophage DNA is not uniform in the lysogenic cell and (2) the transcription of the prophage is restricted to a small number of genes that encode functions that are beneficial to the lysogen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the lysogenic lifestyle of temperate phages in lactic streptcocci.
the molecular mechanisms of lysogeny, the interaction between temperate phages and bacterial hosts and the evolution of temperate phages.
the evolution of temperate phages in low GC content Gram-positives, in particular in streptococcal species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

temperate phage genes that are essential to the phage life cycle are transcribed in the lysogenic host, while nonessential genes that are not required for the phage life are not expressed in the lysogenic cell.
the lysogenization by a temperate phage is an evolutionary strategy of phage to increase the ecological fitness and survival chances of the phage.
prophage transcription in S. thermophiles is very similar to that of temperate phages in other low GC Gram-positive bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
temperate phage genes are not necessarily essential for the survival of the host and that prophage genes may be deleted from the host genome while the host genome is still transcribing them.
temperate phage genomes are not static but rather dynamic entities that are constantly evolving in response to selection pressures exerted by their hosts and the environment.
temperate phage genomes are not static but are constantly evolving by deletion and acquisition of DNA segments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
temperate phage genomes can be divided into a core genome and a variable region.
temperate phage genomes are dynamic entities that change their composition in a way that is beneficial for their host bacteria.
the transcriptional analysis of temperate phages in the prophage state is an important step towards a better understanding of their role in the biology of the host bacterium.
